Alex: Just finished a full pass with the model-equalizer harness across four model builds; P99 spikes on requests that hit the KV cache hot path. dumping run cmd + short logs below.
Alex: Command I used:
```
./harness/run_equalizer --models mA,mB,mC,mD --replay=workspace/replays/long-dialogue.json --decoding 'temp=0.0,top_p=0.95,seed=42' --batcher-config configs/batcher/default.yaml --kernels auto
```

Sam: Do we know which kernel selection branch `auto` picked? v2 vs v3 makes a big diff on causal-attn for long context.
Alex: It picked `fused_attention_v3` for mA,mB but fell back to `fused_attention_v2` for mC because of a different block size. Perf snippet: 
```
KV_hit_rate: 0.72
avg_batch_size: 6.1
kernel_selected: fused_attention_v3 (mA,mB), fused_attention_v2 (mC)
P50: 32ms
P95: 210ms
P99: 520ms
```

Maria: Quick question — are we 100% aligned on tokenization and stop sequence handling between runs? small tokenizer diffs can change decode length distribution and KV behavior.
Alex: Good call. I used the harness-level tokenizer flag `--tokenizer v2` for all models, and stop seq processed post-decode in the harness. but I didn't force `eos_penalty` or `max_new_tokens` consistently across variants.
Sam: That could explain mismatched tail latencies. Make sure `--max_new_tokens` and `--stop` are identical and that the sampler seeds are the same. otherwise P99 comparisons are apples->oranges.
Jen: Also FYI the batcher heuristics changed in PR #3486 last week — it now biases towards larger micro-batches when kv_hot_ratio > 0.6. If our replay has warm prefixes it could be increasing queueing and P99.
Kai: We should try toggling `REDWOOD_BATCHER_STRATEGY`. Try legacy vs greedy to see difference. e.g.
```
REDWOOD_BATCHER_STRATEGY=legacy ./harness/run_equalizer ...
# vs
REDWOOD_BATCHER_STRATEGY=greedy ./harness/run_equalizer ...
```

Alex: Re-ran with legacy strategy + forcing kernel v3 where possible. Results look better on p99 but still a small regression vs baseline for mC. New snippet:
```
KV_hit_rate: 0.81
avg_batch_size: 4.8
kernel_selected: forced_fused_attention_v3
P50: 30ms
P95: 120ms
P99: 330ms
```

Maria: I'd try a KV warmup pass: replay the first 2 tokens of each conversation to pre-populate cache and then run measurement. That isolates cold-start kv misses from real decode cost.
Sam: +1. Also instrument `kv_cache_evictions` and `kv_read_latency` counters. If eviction spikes, the cache eviction policy might be thrashing between model variants.
Alex: Added `--kv-warmup 2` and extra metrics flags. One more run in progress, uploading artifacts to the perf-bot.
perf-bot: Upload complete: https://artifacts.redwood/perf/1767456789/run-annotated.tar.gz. Summary: delta vs baseline (mC): +18% P99, KV_evictions +42%, avg_batch down 15%. Full traces in the tarball.
Jen: That eviction bump aligns with the new batcher heuristics. Suggest we run a controlled A/B where only the batcher is toggled while keeping kernels fixed to confirm.
Kai: Also check kernel compilation flags: `-O3 -funroll-loops` variation between CI builds caused a tiny perf drift last month. Make sure the runtime build id is pinned in the harness metadata.
Alex: Will run the A/B with: same build, same tokenizer, forced kernels where possible, batcher legacy vs greedy, KV warmup on/off. Will post condensed diff once done. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Sam: Nice next steps. If this reproduces, we can add a regression alert to `perf-regressions` with the exact harness command and artifact link.
